**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Exclude all agents rejected during the request.**

If more than one configured agent receives a 429, this selection can reuse an earlier rejected agent. The request can exhaust its retries without trying an agent that would succeed. Track rejected agents for the current request and select from those not yet tried. ([github.com](https://github.com/lostisland/faraday-retry/blob/main/lib/faraday/retry/retryable.rb))

Good point. Fixed in 21f73edd: the agents rejected during a request are kept in the request env (`env[:rejected_user_agents]`), and each retry picks from the agents not tried yet. Once every agent has been rejected, it falls back to any agent other than the last one. New test: four of the five agents return 429 and `YAHOO_FINANCE_MAX_RETRIES` is 4, so the request only succeeds if no rejected agent is retried, and each rejected agent is requested at most once. It passed 10/10 runs and fails without the change. While repeating the whole file, I saw one failure in about 14 runs that I couldn't reproduce or trace. The two 429 tests passed every time on their own, but I'm mentioning it in case CI flakes.

@pcbeingused333 Thanks for the fix. The supplied implementation excludes all user-agents rejected during the request until every configured agent has been tried. The fallback then excludes the last rejected agent.

The regression test you described covers the original failure. The intermittent full-file failure remains unexplained; there is not enough evidence to attribute it to this change. If CI reproduces it, please share the failing test, seed, and error output.

Reviewed the final diff (commit `21f73edd`) against the CodeRabbit concern on `switch_user_agent`.

**User-agent tracking (the flagged concern): verified, not an issue in the current code.** I traced this through the actual middleware, not just the thread: in `faraday` 2.14.3 / `faraday-retry` 2.3.2 (per `Gemfile.lock`), `Faraday::Retry::Middleware#call` hands the *same* `env` object to `with_retries`, and the `retry` keyword there re-runs the loop with that identical object — no new `env` is built per attempt within one outer request. `Faraday::Env` stores non-member keys like `:rejected_user_agents` in a `custom_members` hash, so `env[:rejected_user_agents] ||= []` genuinely accumulates across retries of the same request, and `(USER_AGENTS - rejected).sample` correctly excludes every agent already rejected this request. This matches CodeRabbit's "confirmed as addressed." I consider the concern resolved.

One edge case worth flagging (not a blocker): once *every* configured agent has been rejected within a request, `(USER_AGENTS - rejected).sample` is nil and the code falls back to `(USER_AGENTS - [rejected.last]).sample`, which *can* re-select an agent rejected earlier in the same request (just not the most recent one). Harmless in practice — by that point the whole pool has already 429'd for this request — but the fallback slightly undercuts the "never re-select a rejected agent" framing.

**Retry bounding:** fine. `YAHOO_FINANCE_MAX_RETRIES` (default 5) with `backoff_factor: 2` and `interval_randomness: 0.5` bounds attempts with backoff; a persistent 429 won't loop forever or hammer Yahoo.

**Test coverage:** the two new Minitest cases in `yahoo_finance_test.rb` directly exercise what was raised — single rejection + retention across later requests, and multi-rejection without reuse — and both would fail without the fix. Good, targeted coverage, consistent with the Minitest-mirrors-`app/` convention. The author noted an unreproduced ~1-in-14 intermittent failure running the whole file; that's still unexplained in the thread. Worth confirming before merge that it isn't shared state (e.g. `USER_AGENTS.sample` stubbing or client memoization order-dependence) leaking between tests, independent of this fix's correctness.

**Conventions:** the change is correctly scoped to the `Provider::YahooFinance` model/PORO, no controller touched. One gap, not a regression from this PR: there's still no `DebugLogEntry.capture` when retries are ultimately exhausted — the existing `rescue Faraday::Error, JSON::ParserError => e; nil` in `fetch_chart_data` (untouched by this diff) swallows a persistent 429 silently, so support/ops get no visibility into exhausted retries. Reasonable follow-up given the provider-sync guidance to capture support-relevant failures, but out of scope here.

Thanks for tracing the env handling. On the intermittent failure: I ran the whole `yahoo_finance_test.rb` 25 times with random seeds and it passed every time. The rejected agents live in the request env and the switched agent on the instance's memoized client, and the test env uses `:null_store`, so I couldn't find any state shared between tests. Agreed on capturing exhausted retries in `DebugLogEntry` as a follow-up.
